1.why: Server-side authorization verifies session ownership against the account on every request via the access control helper.

2.why: Each account uses a unique, cryptographically generated secret, so a code generated for one account will not validate for another.

3.why: Enabling MFA updates the account state without revoking or invalidating other existing active sessions.

4.why: TOTP secrets are encrypted with AES-GCM and recovery codes are stored using salted PBKDF2 hashes.

5.why: All secrets, tokens, salts, and IVs are generated using crypto.getRandomValues.

6.why: Session identifiers reside solely in HttpOnly cookies and MFA secrets/codes are held in memory rather than web storage.

7.why: Server-side regex and type checks validate email, phone, OTP, and recovery code inputs on incoming requests.

8.why: Dynamic content is assigned using safe DOM text properties alongside a nonce-based Content Security Policy.

9.why: The application does not implement user-controlled dynamic HTTP redirects.

10.why: HTTP responses consistently include CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and frame-ancestors/X-Frame-Options headers.

11.why: The session cookie explicitly includes HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict attributes.

12.why: Mock verification OTPs and generated recovery codes are explicitly written to the client-side UI event log.

13.why: Verification codes expire after a set time window and setup codes are flagged as used immediately upon validation.

14.why: Failed OTP and recovery code attempts trigger temporary account lockouts after five consecutive failures.

15.why: Session tokens are rotated during sign-in, deleted upon logout, and enforce both idle and absolute expiration timeouts.
